translationRepairs: In the first year of Yongchun (682), famine afflicted Guanzhong and twenty-six prefectures south of the mountains; in the capital people resorted to cannibalism.
In the first year of Yongchun (682), famine afflicted Guanzhong and twenty-six prefectures of Shannan; in the capital people resorted to cannibalism.
山南 is the Shannan circuit, set parallel to Guanzhong, not a generic 'south of the mountains'. The literal already says Shannan.

In its effect upon the world it resembles a ruler's proclamation; stirring through heaven and earth, it sometimes raises flying sand and dust in anger, and when it tears off roofs and uproots trees, its wrath is extreme.

In its effect on things it resembles a ruler's proclamation; stirring through heaven and earth, it sometimes raises flying sand and dust in anger, and when it tears off roofs and uproots trees, its wrath is extreme.
及物 means the wind's effect on things. 'Upon the world' changes the object.
It also says: "When gusting wind enters the palace gates, three or four times in a day, and if the sound of wind like thunder strikes the ground and rises, armies will arise."
It also says: "When gusting wind enters the palace gates, two or three times in a day, and if the sound of wind like thunder strikes the ground and rises, armies will arise."
一日再三 is two or three times in a day, not three or four.
When Cui Xuanwei was enfeoffed as Prince of Boling, a great wind broke the canopy of his carriage.
When Cui Xuanwei was enfeoffed as Prince of Boling Commandery, a great wind broke the canopy of his carriage.
博陵郡王 is a commandery prince. The idiomatic drops 郡, which the literal keeps.

In the tenth month, a great wind in Xiazhou piled flying sand into heaps as high as the city battlements.
夏州 is Xiazhou (Xia Prefecture). Xizhou would be a different name.

In the sixth month of the eleventh year of Tianbao (752), the tomb of Nüwa in the Yellow River at Yinyi in Guozhou was lost to sight in heavy rain and murky darkness; then on the night of the sixth month of the second year of Qianyuan (759), the yiwei day, people along the river heard wind and thunder, and at dawn saw the tomb thrust up from the water; beneath it lay a great stone, and upon it stood twin willows, each more than a zhang tall; at the time it was called Fengling Mound.
